  • paired dashboard · 02

    Paired: a dashboard and its data, in two files

    dash.html is a dashboard with no data inside it. The rows live in data.js beside it, and the page loads that file. Replace data.js in a synced folder and everyone who has the pair sees the new numbers without anyone rebuilding the page.

    Byggekommandopython3 tools/build_dashboard.py \ --data examples/01-hello-dashboard/salgsdata.csv \ --title "Salg per region og produkt 2026" \ --dimension Produkt --measure Belop --time Maaned \ --filters Region,Produkt,Kanal \ --source "Eksempeldata (syntetisk) — salgsdata.csv" \ --requested-by "Prosjekteier" \ --mode paired \ --out examples/02-paired-dashboard/dash.html

  • xlsx from file · 22

    Reading a real .xlsx from file://, with no library

    An .xlsx is a ZIP archive holding SpreadsheetML XML. xlsx-from-file.html unpacks one with nothing but what a modern browser already ships: DecompressionStream('deflate-raw') to inflate each ZIP entry, and DOMParser to read the XML parts. No xlsx library, no bundler, one file.

  • survey crosstab · 31

    Two questions at once, and why that has an all-or-nothing rule

    A survey board counts one question at a time. The moment someone asks "and how do those two answers line up", the arithmetic changes: multiplying two questions is exactly how a small group becomes a nameable person, so a cross-tab needs its own rule rather than the per-cell floor the rest of the board uses.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/31-survey-crosstab/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_survey_dashboard.py \ --data examples/31-survey-crosstab/survey-wide.csv --wide \ --questions "Jeg får svar på det jeg spør om,Verktøyene jeg bruker passer til oppgaven,Jeg vet hvem som bestemmer i saken,Jeg har fått opplæring i verktøyene" \ --cross "Jeg får svar på det jeg spør om|Verktøyene jeg bruker passer til oppgaven" \ --cross "Jeg vet hvem som bestemmer i saken|Jeg har fått opplæring i verktøyene" \ --segments Enhet,Rolle \ --title "Arbeidsmiljø 2026 — krysstabeller" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (survey-wide.csv)" \ --requested-by "HR" \ --out examples/31-survey-crosstab/survey-crosstab.html

  • comparison · 33

    "What moved since last month"

    Half of the reporting a tenant does is a subtraction. Two extracts of the same measure, one per period, matched on a key, and the reader wants to know what moved, by how much, and what is new or gone. That work is done by hand in Excel, where the arithmetic is invisible, the result dies with the spreadsheet, and nobody can see afterwards whether a key was dropped on the way.

  • review roundtrip · 36

    The file that answers back

    Every other artefact in this repository is one-way. Someone opens it, disagrees with a number, and the only route back is a screenshot and a sentence naming neither the row nor the build: "tallet for mars ser feil ut", when the file holds 96 rows and three builds exist. Here the file asks. The reader presses one button, clicks the row, writes a comment, and copies a single text block. On the other side a tool reads the block, finds the row again, and puts the file's own number next to the reader's.

  • distribution · 38

    The shape of the data, not its total

    Every other artefact this engine builds answers a question about a total. A total says nothing about whether a typical case is typical: three cases of 1, 1 and 40 days have the same sum as eleven cases of 4, and an average of 14 describes neither. Case handling time, claim size, transaction amount, response time: the same thing is true of all of them, and the figure people quote is the one the shape makes misleading.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/38-distribution/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_distribution.py \ --data examples/38-distribution/saksbehandlingstid.csv \ --measure-col Dager \ --group-col Enhet \ --title "Saksbehandlingstid per enhet" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (saksbehandlingstid.csv)" \ --requested-by "Fagavdelingen" \ --out examples/38-distribution/behandlingstid.html
  • scorecard · 39

    Many measures, one period, with their targets

    The monthly management report has the same shape almost everywhere: a short list of measures, each with this period's figure, the change, the target and a status. Two things make it useful, and neither existed in this repository before this artefact: a trend small enough to sit beside the number, and a target to be measured against.

  • waterfall · 40

    The steps that add up to a change

    Reporting usually stops at "the number went from 12,1 to 13,1 million". The next question is always the same: which parts account for it, and do they add up? That answer lives in a spreadsheet somebody keeps by hand, where the arithmetic is invisible and the total is whatever the last person typed. Here it is an artefact: one self-contained file where every step is drawn, every contributor is written out with its own two figures, and the column adds up on the page.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/40-waterfall/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_waterfall.py \ --data examples/40-waterfall/omsetning.csv \ --measure Omsetning --dim Produkt --period-col Måned \ --from September --to Oktober \ --title "Omsetning per produkt: september mot oktober" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (omsetning.csv)" \ --requested-by "Innsikt" \ --out examples/40-waterfall/bro.html
  • composition · 41

    What the total is made of, and where the mix and the level disagree

    Every artefact before this one answers a question about a level (a dashboard), a change in it (timeline, comparison, waterfall), or the shape of one measure (distribution). None answers the question a management report asks most often: what is this total made of, and how did the mix move?

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/41-composition/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_composition.py \ --data examples/41-composition/bemanning.csv \ --measure Timer --cat Oppgave --period-col Kvartal \ --title "Hva timene gikk til: 2026" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (bemanning.csv)" \ --requested-by "Bemanningskontoret" \ --out examples/41-composition/sammensetning.html
  • funnel · 42

    How many reach each stage, and where the cohort leaks

    Most operational reporting is a funnel: how many cases start, how many get assessed, how many are decided, how many are paid out. It is drawn badly almost everywhere, in two ways. The stages are inferred from the data rather than declared, so the order is a guess presented as a fact. And the drop between two stages is left as a gap in a picture, when the number a reader actually wants is the difference.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/42-funnel/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_funnel.py \ --data examples/42-funnel/soknader.csv \ --id Soknadsnr --stage Status \ --stages "Mottatt,Vurdert,Innstilt,Utbetalt" \ --title "Søknader gjennom behandlingen" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (soknader.csv)" \ --requested-by "Saksbehandlingen" \ --out examples/42-funnel/tratt.html
  • heatmap · 43

    Where the mass is, and where there is none

    A heatmap is the easiest artefact in this repository to draw wrongly, because every mistake is invisible in a screenshot. A shade nobody can convert back into a number. A legend whose ranges do not match the shades actually used. An empty cell drawn as zero. A ramp that has no direction. White text on a pale cell. Each one looks fine and each one lies.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/43-heatmap/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_heatmap.py \ --data examples/43-heatmap/henvendelser.csv \ --row Enhet --col Uke --measure Antall \ --title "Henvendelser per enhet og uke" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (henvendelser.csv)" \ --requested-by "Kundeservice" \ --out examples/43-heatmap/varmekart.html
  • cohort · 44

    Of the people who started, how many are still here

    A cohort grid is the one artefact in this repository whose column axis is not in the file. The columns are periods since each row's own start, derived from every person's first date, and that derivation is where the shape is drawn wrongly almost every time. Each mistake looks completely normal in a screenshot.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/44-cohort/lag_data.py python3 tools/build_cohort.py \ --data examples/44-cohort/kunder.csv \ --id Kunde --date Dato \ --title "Hvor mange blir med videre" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (kunder.csv)" \ --requested-by "Kundeservice" \ --out examples/44-cohort/kohort.html
  • smallmultiples · 45

    Which of these groups behaves differently

    A small multiple is the one chart that answers a comparison question, and it has exactly one requirement: every panel must share a vertical scale. Give each panel its own axis and a group moving between 4 and 8 looks precisely like one moving between 400 and 800. Every number in the picture is still true, the page is beautiful, and the reading is wrong. verifya11y sees nothing, because nothing is unreadable.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/45-smallmultiples/lag_data.py python3 tools/build_smallmultiples.py \ --data examples/45-smallmultiples/ko.csv \ --group Enhet --period Uke --measure Saker \ --title "Saker i ko, per enhet og uke" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (ko.csv)" \ --requested-by "Driftsavdelingen" \ --out examples/45-smallmultiples/smaaflater.html
  • rank change · 46

    Who moved, and how far

    "Who is top now" is a sorted list. "Who moved" is a different question, and a table answers it badly: the reader compares two long columns by eye and gives up somewhere in the middle. Two ranked columns with a line per entity answers it in one glance.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/46-rank-change/lag_data.py python3 tools/build_rank_change.py \ --data examples/46-rank-change/produkter.csv \ --entity Produkt --period Kvartal --measure Omsetning \ --from 2026-K1 --to 2026-K2 \ --title "Hvem klatret, hvem falt" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (produkter.csv)" \ --requested-by "Salg" \ --out examples/46-rank-change/rang.html
  • scatter · 47

    Do these two measures move together

    Every other artefact here answers "how much" or "in what order". This one answers the question behind half the requests that arrive as two columns and no chart: do these two move together, and which unit does not?

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/47-scatter/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_scatter.py \ --data examples/47-scatter/enheter.csv \ --label Enhet --x-col Svartid --y-col Tilfredshet \ --trend \ --title "Svartid mot tilfredshet, per enhet" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (enheter.csv)" \ --requested-by "Kundeservice" \ --out examples/47-scatter/spredning.html
  • boxplot · 48

    Which of these is wide, which is late, and which has a tail

    A distribution per group is the honest answer to "how long does this take", and it stops working at about six groups: six histograms is a wall. A box plot puts twenty groups on one axis, which is the only shape here that answers the question for a whole list at once.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/48-boxplot/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_boxplot.py \ --data examples/48-boxplot/saksbehandlingstid.csv \ --value Dager --group Enhet \ --title "Saksbehandlingstid per enhet" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (saksbehandlingstid.csv)" \ --requested-by "Fagavdelingen" \ --out examples/48-boxplot/boksplott.html
  • gantt · 49

    Was the plan kept, and by how much did it slip

    A timeline (35) shows when things happen. This shows whether the plan held: for every task, one bar for what was planned and one for what happened, on the same date axis, with the difference printed as a signed number of days.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/49-gantt/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_gantt.py \ --data examples/49-gantt/fremdrift.csv \ --task Tiltak --start Planstart --end Planferdig \ --actual-start Faktisk-start --actual-end Faktisk-ferdig \ --today 2026-10-26 \ --title "Fremdrift per tiltak" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (fremdrift.csv)" \ --requested-by "Prosjektkontoret" \ --out examples/49-gantt/fremdrift.html
  • calendar · 50

    When in the week, and when in the year

    A heatmap (43) compares two categories. This compares days: one cell per day, aligned to weekday rows, so "Mondays are always bad" and "August is quiet" become shapes instead of two hundred rows of a table.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/50-calendar/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_calendar.py \ --data examples/50-calendar/hendelser.csv \ --date Dato --value Antall --clamp 40 \ --title "Hendelser per dag, 2026" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (hendelser.csv)" \ --requested-by "Driftsavdelingen" \ --out examples/50-calendar/kalender.html
  • bullet · 51

    Which of these is behind its target

    A scorecard (39) judges a handful of measures over time. This judges a list: fourteen units, each with a number and its own target, and the question is which of them is off plan. A table of two columns makes the reader do the subtraction; a bar chart with no target line hides the only thing that matters.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/51-bullet/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_bullet.py \ --data examples/51-bullet/dekning.csv \ --label Enhet --value Dekning --target Maal --direction up \ --target-note "styremøtet 12.05.2026" \ --title "Dekning mot mål per enhet" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (dekning.csv)" \ --requested-by "Fagavdelingen" \ --out examples/51-bullet/dekning.html
  • pareto · 52

    Which few explain most of it

    A composition (41) asks what a total is made of and draws every part. This asks which parts matter: categories sorted by size, with the cumulative share, and a long tail folded into one bar that carries its count.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/52-pareto/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_pareto.py \ --data examples/52-pareto/henvendelser.csv \ --label Arsak --value Antall \ --title "Henvendelser per årsak" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (henvendelser.csv)" \ --requested-by "Kundesenteret" \ --out examples/52-pareto/arsaker.html
  • sankey · 53

    Where the volume went between stages, and that it adds up

    A funnel (42) counts one cohort through declared stages in a line. This traces volume through a network: several starts, several ends, flows that meet in the middle. The question is where the volume went, and the picture is only worth having if it is arithmetically true.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/53-sankey/generate_data.py python3 tools/build_sankey.py \ --data examples/53-sankey/kanaler.csv \ --from Kanal --to Utfall --value Antall \ --title "Hvor ble henvendelsene av" \ --source "Syntetisk eksempeldata (kanaler.csv)" \ --requested-by "Kundesenteret" \ --out examples/53-sankey/kanaler.html
  • functional app · 55 +1

    When a small server adds value

    Tún's standalone artefacts are the right default for sharing a snapshot. They do not share writes between readers. This example shows the boundary: a small local decision/action log with persistent create and complete operations, followed by a read-only standalone export of the same rows.

    Byggekommandopython3 examples/55-functional-app/app.py serve \ --db work/functional-app/decisions.db \ --seed

Hver fil er en egen, selvstendig HTML-fil. Den åpnes fra en delt mappe, uten server og uten lisens.

Hver fil bærer sitt eget opphav: kjeldedata, uttrekkstid, byggetid og hvem som ba om den.
